context: Tests whether the agent captures a distinctive voice (short declarative sentences, second person, dry humor, a closing instruction, never a bulleted list) with quoted evidence, verbatim passages, varied anti-examples and the writer's absences.

checklist.name: Names short declarative sentences with a quote
checklist.description: The guide names short, declarative sentences as a habit and backs it with a quotation that appears in the samples, such as 'You fill it to the line.' or 'You do not honk.'

checklist.name: Names second-person address with a quote
checklist.description: The guide names direct address to the reader as 'you' as a habit and backs it with a quotation that appears in the samples.

checklist.name: Names dry humor with a quote
checklist.description: The guide names dry, deadpan or understated humor as a habit and backs it with a quotation that appears in the samples, such as 'Honking is for people who still believe in justice.'

checklist.name: Notices no bulleted lists
checklist.description: The guide states that the writer never uses bulleted or numbered lists in the pieces, and says what the writer does instead, such as short paragraphs of prose.

checklist.name: Notices other absences
checklist.description: The guide names at least one more thing the writer never does that the samples show, such as no jargon, no greeting or sign-off, no hedging, no exclamation marks, or no long subordinate clauses.

checklist.name: Five representative passages
checklist.description: The guide presents five representative passages, each with a note on what makes it characteristic.

checklist.name: Passages are verbatim
checklist.description: Every passage presented as representative appears word for word in the sample files. Paraphrased or invented passages presented as the writer's own score zero.

checklist.name: Five anti-examples that break the voice differently
checklist.description: The guide includes five written passages that deliberately break the voice, each breaking it in a different way (for example formal, bulleted, buzzword-heavy, warm and effusive, long-winded), and each has a stated reason it does not fit.

checklist.name: Usable without the samples
checklist.description: The guide includes dos and don'ts or quick reference rules specific enough that someone who has not read the samples could write in this voice.
